text: We tested temperature-scaling of the weak supervisor's soft targets, with a target temperature of 0.5, in a weak-to-strong generalization setup using gpt2-small as the weak supervisor and mistral-7b as the strong student, across 10 seeds. The weak supervisor reached 0.51 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.70, while the temperature-scaled transfer run reached 0.58 accuracy with a standard error of 0.02. The resulting performance gap recovered was 0.39, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.37. Because the PGR standard error is 0.13, the difference between the measured PGR and the baseline falls well within two standard errors, so this experiment does not establish that temperature scaling helps; the observed ordering is compatible with noise. The transfer accuracy estimate is considerably more precise than the PGR estimate, suggesting that PGR variability here stems largely from the ratio's sensitivity rather than from accuracy measurement. Larger seed counts would be needed to resolve an effect of this magnitude.
